headline: Presidential election: BNP collects two nomination papers
summary: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party has taken nomination forms from the Election Commission for the 23rd presidential election.
details: The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has collected two nomination papers from the Election Commission (EC) for the 23rd presidential election.
BNP Vice Chairman Nurul Islam Moni and Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi collected the papers this morning from the EC headquarters in Agargaon, Dhaka.
The development was confirmed by Muhammad Ashraful Alam, personal secretary to Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin.
Bangladesh will elect its 23rd president on August 20, with voting scheduled from 2:00pm to 5:00pm.
Nomination papers must be submitted by August 13, with scrutiny beginning on August 16 and the deadline for withdrawal being August 18.
The EC has already received the 349-member electoral roll from the Parliament Secretariat.
The presidency became vacant after Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned on July 24, with Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad currently serving as acting president.
caption:
The BNP has officially entered the race for the 23rd presidential election by collecting two nomination papers.

The Bangladesh Nationalist Party (BNP) has collected two nomination papers from the Election Commission (EC) for the 23rd presidential election.

BNP Vice Chairman Nurul Islam Moni and Senior Joint Secretary General Ruhul Kabir Rizvi collected the papers this morning from the EC headquarters in Agargaon, Dhaka.

The development was confirmed by Muhammad Ashraful Alam, personal secretary to Chief Election Commissioner AMM Nasir Uddin.

Bangladesh will elect its 23rd president on August 20, with voting scheduled from 2:00pm to 5:00pm.

Nomination papers must be submitted by August 13, with scrutiny beginning on August 16 and the deadline for withdrawal being August 18.

The EC has already received the 349-member electoral roll from the Parliament Secretariat.

The presidency became vacant after Mohammed Shahabuddin resigned on July 24, with Speaker Hafiz Uddin Ahmad currently serving as acting president.

headline_marked: LDP Chairman [[Col (retd) Oli Ahmed nominated as presidential candidate]] by 11-party alliance
headline: LDP Chairman Col (retd) Oli Ahmed nominated as presidential candidate by 11-party alliance
summary: The Jamaat-led alliance nominated the freedom fighter and experienced politician for the August 20 election, citing the need for a competitive and participatory process.
details: Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) Chairman Col (retd) Oli Ahmed has been nominated as the common candidate of the Jamaat-led 11-party alliance for the upcoming presidential election on August 20.
The announcement was made by Opposition Chief Whip and National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener Nahid Islam during a briefing at the official residence of Jamaat chief Shafiqur Rahman in Dhaka.

The alliance stated that the nomination was intended to send a message in favor of a competitive and participatory presidential election, as an opportunity for a consensus candidate had not materialized.
Nahid Islam criticized the government for allegedly politicizing state institutions, including the Election Commission, and disregarding the referendum verdict.
Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis ameer Mamunul Haque described Oli Ahmed as a suitable and highly qualified candidate for the presidency.
Col (retd) Oli Ahmed expressed gratitude to the alliance, stating that his priority is to protect the interests of the people regardless of the election outcome.
Jamaat chief Shafiqur Rahman emphasized that fielding a candidate is part of the alliance's responsibility to uphold democracy and ensure political transparency.
caption:
Col (retd) Oli Ahmed is the 11-party alliance's choice for President. The move aims to push for a competitive election process.

Liberal Democratic Party (LDP) Chairman Col (retd) Oli Ahmed has been nominated as the common candidate of the Jamaat-led 11-party alliance for the upcoming presidential election on August 20.

The announcement was made by Opposition Chief Whip and National Citizen Party (NCP) Convener Nahid Islam during a briefing at the official residence of Jamaat chief Shafiqur Rahman in Dhaka.

The alliance stated that the nomination was intended to send a message in favor of a competitive and participatory presidential election, as an opportunity for a consensus candidate had not materialized.

Nahid Islam criticized the government for allegedly politicizing state institutions, including the Election Commission, and disregarding the referendum verdict.

Bangladesh Khelafat Majlis ameer Mamunul Haque described Oli Ahmed as a suitable and highly qualified candidate for the presidency.

Col (retd) Oli Ahmed expressed gratitude to the alliance, stating that his priority is to protect the interests of the people regardless of the election outcome.

Jamaat chief Shafiqur Rahman emphasized that fielding a candidate is part of the alliance's responsibility to uphold democracy and ensure political transparency.
